content.comment_body: Hello, I'm currently working on a [product_name] project and have hit the block limit several times. I'm cleaning up the program and want to know how many logic blocks are available—does anyone know if you can check the block count somewhere in the application, or is it only visible when the limit is reached? ([product_name] [product_name] [version_no] - [product_name] model FS4) EDIT: I found the information I needed; you can check current memory usage by selecting: Tools -> Determine [product_name]
Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. If you press F2, an information window will open. You'll see an animated icon in the bottom-right corner.

analysis.insight_summary: The user wanted a way to monitor the number of logic blocks used in their [product_name] project to prevent reaching hardware limitations. Initially, they couldn't find a function to display the current block count and requested assistance. Eventually, they located a feature in the software that shows memory usage, and another user suggested a shortcut to access this information quickly.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the software to provide a straightforward feature showing both the number of logic blocks currently used and those still available, to help streamline project management.
